question: What is the main job of a nursing unit manager?

options.A: Handling only the financial accounts of the hospital
options.B: Balancing bedside clinical care with administrative duties
options.C: Writing national health policies for the ministry
options.D: Performing all surgical procedures in the ward

explanation: You've got this! A unit manager wears two caps: they keep an eye on patient care at the bedside while also managing the paperwork and admin tasks that keep the ward running.

question: Why does a unit manager need to understand both patient advocacy and hospital rules?

options.A: To avoid ever having to care for patients directly
options.B: To replace the hospital director when they are away
options.C: To enforce rules while still protecting patient and staff welfare
options.D: To ensure the hospital makes a profit on every bed

explanation: Spot on! The manager acts like a bridge—they make sure hospital guidelines are followed, but they also stand up to protect the safety and rights of both patients and staff.

question: Which of these is a key administrative duty for a nursing unit manager?

options.A: Designing new blueprints for hospital buildings
options.B: Serving as the legal defense attorney for the hospital
options.C: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs for the pharmacy
options.D: Conducting regular performance appraisals for ward staff

explanation: Great job! Doing performance reviews helps managers guide their team members, support their growth, and keep ward standards high.

question: How does mentorship from a unit manager help newly qualified nurses?

options.A: It exempts them from working night shifts
options.B: It guarantees they will never make a clinical mistake
options.C: It helps them transition from students to confident practitioners
options.D: It allows them to bypass hospital safety protocols

explanation: Exactly! Stepping out of the classroom and onto the ward can feel scary. Good mentorship gives new nurses the guidance and boost they need to feel confident.

question: Why do wards track specific numbers like infection rates?

options.A: To reduce the number of patients admitted to the ward
options.B: To punish nurses who work too slowly
options.C: To ensure quality assurance and patient safety
options.D: To increase the cost of hospital admission fees

explanation: You're doing great! Tracking these numbers helps the unit spot safety risks early so they can keep patient care safe and top-notch.

question: What is the best first step for a unit manager when an unexpected error happens on the ward?

options.A: Hide the incident report from the hospital board
options.B: Lead an investigation to find the root cause
options.C: Immediately dismiss the nurse on duty
options.D: Close the entire ward to new admissions

explanation: Spot on! Quality care is all about finding out *why* something went wrong so the system can be fixed, rather than just pointing fingers at individuals.

question: What must a unit manager consider when making a fair duty roster?

options.A: Patient acuity and staff skill mix
options.B: The distance of each nurse's house from the hospital
options.C: The personal fashion preferences of nurses
options.D: Only the seniority of the nurses

explanation: Exactly! A good roster looks at how sick the patients are (acuity) and matches them with nurses who have the right skills for the job.

question: A ward has very sick patients and several junior nurses on duty. What is the best staffing approach?

options.A: Pair junior nurses with experienced senior nurses
options.B: Send all the junior nurses home to rest
options.C: Ignore the patient acuity levels when scheduling
options.D: Assign all critical patients to the most junior nurse

explanation: You got it! Teaming up junior nurses with experienced seniors keeps patients safe and helps the junior staff learn safely.

question: Why do unit managers keep a close eye on daily supplies and medications?

options.A: To sell extra medications to patients for extra cash
options.B: To keep the storage room locked permanently
options.C: To prevent shortages and reduce unnecessary waste
options.D: To ensure the ward has zero items stored at any time

explanation: Spot on! Keeping track of inventory makes sure the ward always has what it needs without wasting valuable hospital supplies.

question: How do unit managers usually help with hospital budgeting?

options.A: By setting the salaries for all doctors in the country
options.B: By deciding which private bank holds hospital funds
options.C: By predicting future equipment and supply needs for their ward
options.D: By collecting taxes from patients upon discharge

explanation: Great thinking! Managers know their wards best, so they help the finance team by forecasting what materials and tools their department will need.

question: Which of these helps maintain a safe physical environment in a nursing unit?

options.A: Removing all clocks so patients lose track of time
options.B: Painting the ward walls in bright neon colors
options.C: Checking that emergency equipment is fully functional
options.D: Locking all windows to prevent fresh air circulation

explanation: Exactly! Regular checks ensure that when a patient suddenly crashes, all the emergency gear is ready to use instantly.

question: Besides physical safety, what else helps create a healing ward environment?

options.A: Playing loud music to keep patients awake during the day
options.B: Keeping the lights at maximum brightness twenty-four hours a day
options.C: Allowing visitors to stay without any time limits
options.D: Reducing noise and addressing patient grievances promptly

explanation: You've got this! Healing isn't just physical—lowering stress by keeping noise down and listening to patient complaints makes a huge difference.

question: What is a major benefit of good teamwork and communication on a ward?

options.A: It eliminates the need for patient medical records
options.B: It ensures nurses never have to speak with doctors
options.C: It allows the ward to close earlier every evening
options.D: It helps prevent medical errors and streamlines treatment

explanation: Spot on! When doctors, nurses, and other health workers talk clearly, everyone stays on the same page and mistakes are easily avoided.

question: What should a unit manager do when staff members have a workplace conflict?

options.A: Reporting both workers to the police immediately
options.B: Acting as a mediator to restore a collaborative working relationship
options.C: Taking sides with the senior doctor against the nurses
options.D: Encouraging the staff members to stop speaking entirely

explanation: Great job! A good manager steps in to help sort out friction, keeping the team united and the working environment safe for everyone.

question: Which factor contributes heavily to nursing staff shortages in many Nigerian health units?

options.B: The migration of experienced nurses abroad
options.D: A complete lack of nursing training schools

explanation: You're spot on. The 'japa' wave has caused many skilled nurses to move abroad for better opportunities, leaving local units short-staffed.

question: How do effective unit managers keep patients safe during tough staff and resource shortages?

options.A: By charging patients exorbitant fees for basic cotton wool
options.B: By pretending that the shortages do not exist at all
options.C: By turning away every single patient who walks through the door
options.D: By using creative resourcefulness and strong advocacy skills

explanation: Brilliant! Even when resources are tight, resourceful managers find safe workarounds and fight hard for what their ward needs.
